briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-005
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- warehouse roof: (114, 43), roof
- control room: (30, -34), indoor
- loading dock: (109, -104), outdoor
- transformer pad: (73, -139), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3420 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 5 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3600 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 960 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Photograph transformer pad for the condition report. Location: transformer pad. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T2: Run a thermal scan of loading dock. Location: loading dock. Duration: 210 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T3: Inspect warehouse roof with a camera. Location: warehouse roof. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.
- T4: Run a thermal scan of loading dock. Location: loading dock. Duration: 150 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 540 s.
- T5: Inspect warehouse roof with a camera. Location: warehouse roof. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 1200 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: warehouse roof (114, 43, a rooftop); control room (30, -34, indoors); loading dock (109, -104, outside); transformer pad (73, -139, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 57 minutes including getting back. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 5 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 60 minutes including getting back. D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera and a thermal camera, cruises at 7.5 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 16 minutes of flight time, return trip included.

Jobs:
(T1) Document transformer pad with pictures - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T2) Look for overheating equipment around loading dock - that takes 3.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Do a visual check of warehouse roof - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.
(T4) Look for overheating equipment around loading dock - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 9 minutes.
(T5) Get eyes on warehouse roof and check the panels - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 20 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
